job.style: a rule explained with two contrasting examples

passage: In geometry, understanding the properties of lines and angles requires precision. A line is defined as having no endpoints, extending infinitely in both directions, whereas a line segment is a distinct part of a line with two fixed endpoints. When two lines intersect, the vertically opposite angles formed are always equal, not supplementary. For example, if two lines cross and one angle is 70 degrees, the angle opposite to it is also 70 degrees, not 110 degrees. Furthermore, the sum of the interior angles of any triangle is always exactly 180 degrees, regardless of the triangle's size or whether it is acute, right, or obtuse. Consider a tiny triangle and a massive triangle drawn on a large field; both will have an angle sum of 180 degrees. Finally, for two lines to be considered parallel, they must never meet, even if extended infinitely. This property holds true regardless of their orientation; lines can be parallel whether they are horizontal, vertical, or tilted at an angle. If a transversal cuts two lines, they are only parallel if specific conditions, such as equal corresponding angles, are met. Visual appearance is never enough to confirm parallelism; geometric proof is required.

items.evidence: When two lines intersect, the vertically opposite angles formed are always equal, not supplementary.
items.q: Two lines cross and one angle is 40 degrees. What is the angle opposite to it?
items.explain: Vertically opposite angles are always equal, so the opposite angle is also 40 degrees.

wrong.why: thinks vertically opposite angles add up to 180 degrees
thinks the two angles add up to 90 degrees
subtracts from a full turn of 360 degrees

items.evidence: Consider a tiny triangle and a massive triangle drawn on a large field; both will have an angle sum of 180 degrees.
items.q: A very big triangle is marked out on a playground. What do its three angles add up to?
options: Exactly 180 degrees, like a small one
More than 180 degrees, since it is bigger
Less than 180 degrees, since sides are long
items.explain: A triangle's angles always add up to 180 degrees, whatever its size.

wrong.why: thinks bigger triangles have bigger angle sums
thinks long sides make the angles smaller
mixes up a triangle with a quadrilateral

items.evidence: A line is defined as having no endpoints, extending infinitely in both directions, whereas a line segment is a distinct part of a line with two fixed endpoints.
items.q: How is a line different from a line segment?
options: A line has no ends; a segment has two
A line has two ends; a segment has none
Both have two ends; a line is longer
A line has one end; a segment has two
items.explain: A line goes on forever in both directions, but a segment has two fixed endpoints.

wrong.why: thinks a line has two end points like a segment
mixes up a line with a ray

items.evidence: If a transversal cuts two lines, they are only parallel if specific conditions, such as equal corresponding angles, are met.
items.q: Two lines look parallel in a drawing. How can Meena prove that they really are?
options: By checking angles made by a transversal
By seeing that they look evenly spaced
By checking that both lines are horizontal
By checking that both have the same length
items.explain: Looks are never enough; lines are parallel only if conditions like equal corresponding angles hold.

wrong.why: trusts how the lines look in the figure
thinks parallel lines must be horizontal
confuses parallel lines with equal segments
